programs.title: GAS, replication, and data
programs.summary: Three short steps, then the courses for Gameplay Ability System, replication, and data-driven design.

choices: By gameplay tag through the ability system.
By Cast To the ability Blueprint.

compares.title: Tag or a cast
compares.note: This path activates by gameplay tag. A cast chain grows every time you add an ability.

left.label: Cast chain
left.body:
Cast to BP_Dash.
Cast to BP_Heal.
Each new ability edits the character.

right.label: Gameplay tag
right.body:
The ability system activates by tag.
Cost and cooldown are checked there.
The character does not cast to each ability.

nodes.title: Input
nodes.detail: The key asks the ability system. It does not apply damage itself.

nodes.title: Interaction
nodes.detail: An interface reaches the actor. A cast list does not.

nodes.title: Health
nodes.detail: Authority writes health. OnRep tells the UI.

nodes.title: UI
nodes.detail: The widget reads a data table row and OnRep. It does not own the rules.

starter.summary: A health component the courses can build on. Authority writes health.
starter.when_to_use: Use this starter when you want one replicated health component before you add GAS or a data table.
starter.common_mistakes: A common mistake is to change health on the client, or to put the number only in the widget.

courses.title: GAS basics
courses.summary: The ability system, attributes, activating by tag, and effects. Scores stay on this computer.

modules.title: The ability system
modules.takeaway: The ability system component owns activate, cost, and cooldown. The character does not.

assignment.prompt: Name the component that activates abilities.

quiz.prompt: What owns an ability's cost check?
quiz.why: The ability system checks cost before the ability runs.
quiz.review_prompt: Which piece checks an ability's cost?

diff.review_prompt: One of these ability starts is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: Tick skips the cost check the ability system would have done.

modules.title: Attributes
modules.takeaway: Health as an attribute is one number the ability system can change. Do not keep a second health float.

assignment.prompt: Where does this course keep health?

quiz.why: The attribute set is the number effects change.

diff.review_prompt: One health store is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: A second float drifts away from the attribute.

modules.title: Activate by tag
modules.takeaway: Activate by gameplay tag so a new ability does not need a new cast.

quiz.prompt: How does this course start an ability?
quiz.why: A tag stays stable when you add another ability.

diff.review_prompt: One start path is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: The cast has to be edited for every new ability.

modules.title: Effects
modules.takeaway: A gameplay effect applies cost and cooldown. Do not subtract the cost by hand as well.

quiz.why: The effect is the cost and the cooldown.

diff.review_prompt: One cost path is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: Subtracting by hand and applying an effect spends the cost twice.

courses.title: Multiplayer replication
courses.summary: Authority, replicated properties, OnRep, and RPCs. Scores stay on this computer.

modules.title: Authority
modules.takeaway: The machine with authority writes shared gameplay state. A client can ask.

quiz.why: If every client writes it, the copies disagree.
quiz.review_prompt: Who is allowed to write replicated health?

diff.review_prompt: One damage path is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: The client path changes health the server did not agree to.

modules.title: Replicated properties
modules.takeaway: Replicate the number. Do not replicate the mesh or the widget.

assignment.prompt: What do you replicate for health?

quiz.prompt: What should replicate for a health bar?
quiz.why: The property is small. The widget is rebuilt on each machine.
quiz.review_prompt: What replicates for the health bar?

diff.review_prompt: One replicated piece is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: Replicating the widget sends the wrong thing.

modules.title: OnRep
modules.takeaway: OnRep is where other machines hear the new value. Play the hit there, do not decide the rule there.

assignment.prompt: What runs when replicated health arrives?

quiz.why: OnRep is the arrival of the property, not a frame loop.

diff.review_prompt: One OnRep is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: OnRep should not apply the damage again.

modules.title: RPCs
modules.takeaway: A server RPC asks. The server function decides. Do not trust the client's number.

assignment.prompt: Which RPC asks the server to act?

quiz.prompt: Which RPC should a client use to ask for damage?
quiz.why: The server RPC is the request. The server still checks it.

diff.review_prompt: One request is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: The multicast writes health on every machine from the client's number.

courses.title: Data-driven design
courses.summary: Data tables, row structs, and data assets. Scores stay on this computer.

modules.title: Data tables
modules.takeaway: A data table is a list of rows designers can edit without a code change.

assignment.prompt: What holds one row per weapon?

quiz.prompt: What is a data table for?
quiz.why: The table is the list. The game reads a row.
quiz.review_prompt: What is a data table for?

diff.review_prompt: One magazine size is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: A hardcoded size ignores the row designers edit.

modules.title: Row struct
modules.takeaway: The row struct is the shape of one table row. It inherits FTableRowBase.

assignment.prompt: What does the row struct inherit?

quiz.prompt: What does a data table row inherit?
quiz.why: FTableRowBase is the row type Unreal expects.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the row struct inherit?

diff.review_prompt: One row type is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: An actor is not a table row.

left.label: Row
left.code: struct FWeaponRow : public FTableRowBase { int32 Magazine; };

modules.title: Data assets
modules.takeaway: A data asset is one item definition: id, mesh reference, and rules. The pickup actor points at it.

assignment.prompt: What kind of asset is one item definition?

quiz.prompt: What is a primary data asset good for here?
quiz.why: The asset is the definition. Many pickups can point at it.
quiz.review_prompt: What is the data asset for?

diff.review_prompt: One item definition is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: Copying the numbers onto every actor drifts.

right.label: Copied numbers
right.code: int32 MaxStack = 10; // pasted on every actor

modules.title: Who reads the row
modules.takeaway: The component reads the row. The widget does not decide magazine size.

assignment.prompt: Who reads the row and applies it?

quiz.prompt: Who should read the weapon row?
quiz.why: The component owns the rule. The widget draws the result.

diff.review_prompt: One reader is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: The widget should not be the authority for magazine size.
